unit.why: A single narrative: R. Zvi Elimelekh of Dinov hears his master's report of a heavenly proclamation and rushes to Kozienice to see the Maggid's face.

stories.start_quote: עוד במכתב הנ"ל וזה"ל סיפר לי
stories.summary_en: At the third Sabbath meal, R. Menahem Mendel of Rymanów reports a heavenly proclamation that whoever lives in the Maggid of Kozienice's generation and does not see him will not see the Messiah. His disciple R. Zvi Elimelekh of Dinov sets out at once, travels without rest straight to the Maggid's room, and strains over the crowd to see him. The Maggid lifts his head and says that mere seeing acquires it.

tags.why: The disciple of the Rymanów rebbe leaves him to see the Maggid of Kozienice.

quotes: ולקח מקלו בידו ותרמילו על כתפו לילך לקאזניץ
tags.why: He journeys to the Maggid's court.
Expectation of the Messiah's imminent coming drives the plot.
Imminent messianic arrival is the motive.
The Rymanów rebbe hears a heavenly proclamation.

quotes: הגביה המגיד ראשו ואמר בראיה בעלמא קני
tags.why: The Maggid responds to the disciple's unspoken purpose.
The proclamation is reported at the third Sabbath meal.

quotes: שבעת הסתופפו בצל הגאוה״ק רבינו מנחם מענדיל
קיבל פרידת שלום מאת רבו הק׳
tags.why: The disciple takes leave of his master to act on his words.

quotes: עמדו סביב מיטתו אשר הי' שוכב שמה הרבה אנשים ונשים

tags.why: The story is framed as an oral transmission chain within a letter.
Merely seeing the tzaddik's face carries spiritual value.
